data.narrative:
Orbit Fab is a Series A-stage space and aerospace company founded by Daniel Faber and Jeremy Schiel that has raised $28.5M to date. The valuation exercise draws from a comp universe of 6 public space and aerospace peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private companies in the sector, though narrowly filtered peers proved insufficient for reliable median benchmarking.

The Stage-Progression method is the primary applicable approach. Using total raised ($28.5M) as a proxy for implied pre-money valuation and applying a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A to follow-on progression yields $57M. The Public-Comp Anchoring method cannot be applied; while the Space & Aerospace sector median P/S is 26.4x across the 5 public comps, Orbit Fab's revenue is not on file, making multiple-based valuation inapplicable. The Peer-Median method similarly does not apply due to an insufficient narrow peer set—only 2 adjacent-stage comparables exist within the filtered universe, below the 3-datapoint threshold for statistical reliability.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $48M to $66M, with a median point of $57M. This range reflects the methodological constraint of relying on a single applicable method. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue disclosure, which precludes multiple-based anchoring to public comps, and limited same-stage private peer data. Confidence in this range is correspondingly moderate.
